diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $A\in\R^{d\times d}$ be skew-symmetric,  $b\in\R^{d}$, and suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.
\bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}

Assumption \ref{assump:dom} is in fact equivalent to the validity of~\eqref{eq:kornetto0}. To see this, note that $\bv\mapsto \norm{\bv\cdot\bn}_{L^{q}(\Gamma)}$ can only fail to be a norm on $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$ provided that there exists $\bv\in\mathcal{R}(\Omega)\setminus\{\b0\}$ such that $\norm{\bv\cdot\bn}_{L^{q}(\Gamma)}=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assump:dom requires that ρ·n = 0 on Γ = Γ₁∪Γ₂ implies ρ = 0 for ρ ∈ 𝓡(Ω). The proof instead assumes the stronger hypothesis ρ = 0 on Γ (i.e., Ax + b = 0 on Γ) and derives ρ = 0. Even under the correct hypothesis ρ·n = 0 on Γ, two non-collinear face normals in d = 3 only force A = 0 and b·n₁ = b·n₂ = 0, leaving b in span(n₁×n₂) possibly nonzero. Concrete counterexample: a triangular prism with cross-section in the x₁x₂-plane extruded in x₃, Γ₁ = {x₁ = 0}-face (normal −e₁) and Γ₂ = {x₂ = 0}-face (normal −e₂). The translation ρ(x) = (0,0,μ) with μ ≠ 0 is a rigid deformation with ρ·n = 0 on Γ₁∪Γ₂ but ρ ≠ 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the corollary's hypothesis to require that the normals ν₁, …, ν_m of the boundary pieces Γ₁, …, Γ_m on Γ span ℝ^d (for d = 3, at least three faces with normals not all coplanar). Rewrite the proof using the correct condition ρ·n = 0 on Γ (not ρ = 0 on Γ), showing An_i = 0 and b·n_i = 0 on each face with normal n_i; spanning normals then force A = 0 and b = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's claim that two non-collinear face normals suffice for Assumption assump:dom is false in d = 3, invalidating the stated scope for mixed boundary conditions in Remark rmk:mixed-bc. The main theorems (thm:main-unsteady, thm:main-unsteady-v) use Γ = ∂Ω where the face normals of any bounded polyhedron span ℝ^d, so Assumption assump:dom does hold there; these results survive.
issues.title: Corollary cor:polyhedral is false for d=3 and its proof verifies the wrong hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The statement must be strengthened (requiring spanning normals rather than merely non-collinear normals) and the proof must be rewritten using the correct hypothesis ρ·n = 0. The main results for Γ = ∂Ω remain valid and the correction is a contained argument; but the advertised generality for mixed boundary conditions in d = 3 is narrowed.
